levels.title: Families
levels.subtitle: Alkali metals, halogens and noble gases
levels.tip: Try this: pop only the elements that belong to the family on the sign. Tap a bubble to pop it. A wrong pop costs a heart and I will tell you what it really is.

rounds.fact: The alkali metals (Li, Na, K, Cs…) are in group 1. Each has one valence electron, so they are soft, shiny and react strongly with water.
The halogens (F, Cl, Br, I) are in group 17. Each has seven valence electrons and gains one electron to form a 1− ion.
The noble gases are in group 18. Their outer shells are full, so they are very unreactive.
The alkaline earth metals (Be, Mg, Ca, Ba) are in group 2. Each has two valence electrons and forms a 2+ ion.

levels.title: Metal or not?
levels.subtitle: Metals, nonmetals and metalloids
levels.tip: Did you know? On the periodic table a zigzag line separates the metals on the left from the nonmetals on the right. The elements touching the line are the metalloids.

rounds.fact: Metalloids (B, Si, Ge, As…) sit along the zigzag line. They have some properties of metals and some of nonmetals.
Nonmetals are on the right of the table (plus hydrogen). They are poor conductors and tend to gain electrons.
Most elements are metals. They conduct electricity, are shiny and tend to lose electrons to form positive ions.
Period 3 runs Na, Mg, Al (metals), Si (metalloid), then P, S, Cl, Ar (nonmetals): it changes from metal to nonmetal across a period.

levels.title: Groups and periods
levels.subtitle: Columns and rows of the table
levels.tip: Try this: a group is a column and a period is a row. Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons.

rounds.fact: Group 17 is the halogens: F, Cl, Br and I. The same column means the same number of valence electrons (7).
Group 14 runs from nonmetal carbon to metals tin and lead. Each has four valence electrons.
Period 3 is the third row: Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl and Ar. Their outer electrons are in the third shell.
Group 1 holds hydrogen and the alkali metals. Hydrogen has one valence electron too, but it is not an alkali metal.

levels.title: Falls Master
levels.subtitle: Boss: everything, against the clock
levels.tip: Boss level! Six rounds, 40 seconds each. Read the sign carefully: some rounds combine two rules, and a near miss costs a heart.

rounds.fact: The d-block is the middle of the table (groups 3 to 12), where the d subshell is being filled. Most are metals.
Group 15 has five valence electrons: N, P, As (and Sb, Bi).
The nonmetals in period 3 are P, S, Cl and Ar.
All four halogens in the game: F, Cl, Br and I, in group 17.
Group 2 is the alkaline earth metals, with two valence electrons each.
Group 13 starts with the metalloid boron; aluminium and gallium below it are metals.
